title: CSES Problem Set digest (post-Striver)
relevance: CSES is the standard bridge from Striver/LC templates to contest constraints; Sorting & Searching + Range Queries + Trees + contest Graphs/DP cover most OA and Div2 C–D patterns Striver never drills in CF form.
company_notes: OA/interview prompts map to CSES patterns: max concurrent users/rooms/servers (Restaurant Customers / Room Allocation sweeps, Amazon/Uber-style scheduling); point update + range sum or first hotel with capacity ≥ x (Dynamic Range Sum / Hotel Queries); shortest path with one coupon (Flight Discount state Dijkstra, Div2 C/D and harder OA); digit-constrained counts in [L,R] or n≤40 subset sum (Counting Numbers digit DP / Meet-in-the-Middle when knapsack or 2^n is the wrong reflex).

phases.goal: Establish that CSES is a section-priority post-Striver curriculum and that OA prompts map to specific CSES pattern families.

must_hit.point: Treat CSES as a section-priority curriculum, not a solve-all-300 grind.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says prioritize sections by placement value rather than clearing the whole set.

must_hit.point: Using CSES right means Striver-like patterns under n≤2e5, multi-query, and writing the template under constraints.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts LC/template comfort with contest-scale I/O and multi-query form.

must_hit.point: Max concurrent users/rooms/servers from intervals maps to Restaurant Customers / Room Allocation sweep patterns.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names arrival/departure sweep or free-room assignment for scheduling screens.

must_hit.point: Shortest path with one coupon/discount maps to Flight Discount state Dijkstra; n≤40 subset sum maps to Meet-in-the-Middle, not forced knapsack.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out expand-node-state graphs and MITM when 2^n is too big.

probes: After Striver, how should you use CSES—and what OA prompt shapes should trigger which CSES patterns?

hints.1: Think curriculum order and OA wording, not problem count.
hints.2: Bridge idea: same algorithms as Striver, contest constraints and multi-query form.
hints.3: Section-priority (not all 300); concurrent intervals → sweep; one coupon → state Dijkstra; n≤40 subset sum → MITM.

phases.goal: Establish the post-Striver section order and which families to do deeply, selectively, or defer.

must_hit.point: Section order: Sorting & Searching (STL/sweep/BS) → DP contest gems → Graphs (state Dijkstra / BF / lifting) → Range Queries (whole section) → Trees (diameter → rerooting → LCA → Euler+BIT) → selective Math/Strings → MITM → then stretch Advanced/Additional.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites that pipeline, especially diameter before rerooting before LCA before Euler+BIT.

must_hit.point: Do deeply: Sorting & Searching, Range Queries, Tree Algorithms, contest Graph flavors, and DP gems (Array Description, Counting Towers, Projects, Elevator Rides, Counting Numbers).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those deep sections and names several DP gems.

must_hit.point: Skip/skim Introductory and easy Sorting warmups that are pure LC; defer Geometry, Additional Problems, Interactive, and most Advanced Techniques until cores are solid (except Meet-in-the-Middle).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicit skip/defer list with MITM as the Advanced exception.

must_hit.point: Range-query ladder: prefix → sparse RMQ → Fenwick PURS → segtree walk → lazy (stretch); Dynamic Range Sum is the entry ticket.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Starts Range Queries at Dynamic Range Sum and climbs Fenwick then segtree walk.

probes: Walk the section order you would follow post-Striver, and what you skip or defer.

hints.1: Start from Sorting & Searching skills, not Introductory grind.
hints.2: Name the deep blocks: Sorting/Searching, DP gems, Graphs, full Range Queries, Trees, then MITM.
hints.3: Order: Sorting & Searching → DP gems → Graphs → Range Queries → Trees → selective Math/Strings → MITM; skip Introductory/Geometry/Additional until cores; MITM is the Advanced must-do exception.

phases.goal: Establish the concrete contest kits: STL/sweep/BS, range structures, tree/graph lifting, and contest DP shapes.

must_hit.point: STL contest kit: multiset with --upper_bound (Concert Tickets: largest ticket ≤ price), sweep events (time, ±1), and a priority queue for free resources (Room Allocation).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes --it after upper_bound, ±1 events, and free-room PQ assignment.

must_hit.point: BS-on-answer reflex: monotone can(mid) as in Factory Machines (“can we make t products by time mid?”), always long long.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States timed production feasibility check and long long habit.

must_hit.point: Graph contest kit: Dijkstra with extra state dist[u][usedCoupon] (Flight Discount); Bellman-Ford plus cycle reachability (High Score); functional binary lifting for k-th successor (Planets Queries I); same jump idea as LCA up[k][v] without a tree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions coupon state, positive-cycle reachability for ∞ score, and functional jumps.

must_hit.point: DP contest kit shapes: dp[i][v] ways for Array Description with |a_i−a_{i+1}|≤1; weighted intervals Projects as sort-by-end dp[i]=max(skip, reward+dp[prev]); Elevator Rides dp[mask]=(rides, last_load); digit DP for Counting Numbers on [a,b] with no adjacent equal digits.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names those DP formulations rather than generic knapsack memo.

probes: For Concert Tickets, Factory Machines, Flight Discount, and Projects, what are the implementation reflexes?

hints.1: Pick one STL, one BS-on-answer, one graph-state, one DP shape.
hints.2: Concert Tickets is multiset upper_bound; Factory Machines is can(mid); Flight Discount expands node state; Projects is weighted intervals with prev via BS.
hints.3: multiset --upper_bound; can(mid) for products by time with long long; dist[u][usedCoupon]; sort by end and dp[i]=max(skip, reward+dp[prev]).

phases.goal: Establish the constraint reflexes that force contest templates: n≤2e5 multi-query form, BS answer range, and n≤40 MITM.

must_hit.point: Under n≤2e5 with multi-query contest form, you write the template (Fenwick/segtree, lifting, sweeps) rather than LC-style one-shot solutions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties n≤2e5 and multi-query to needing the actual DS/template.

must_hit.point: BS-on-answer (Factory Machines) uses monotone can(mid) with answer on [0, 1e18] and long long.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the [0, 1e18] search domain and long long.

must_hit.point: When n≤40 and 2^n is too big, use Meet-in-the-Middle: two halves 2^{n/2}; do not force knapsack DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says split into halves at 2^{n/2} instead of full 2^n or knapsack.

probes: What constraint signals tell you to reach for Fenwick/segtree or MITM instead of a plain LC approach?

hints.1: Look at n and whether queries or subset explosion dominate.
hints.2: n≤2e5 multi-query → range/lifting templates; n≤40 subset sum → MITM.
hints.3: n≤2e5 means write Fenwick/segtree/sweep templates; BS answers live on [0, 1e18] with long long; n≤40 → two halves 2^{n/2}, not knapsack.

phases.goal: Surface skip mistakes, numeric traps, cycle/score traps, and wrong DP/graph reflexes.

must_hit.point: Subarray Sums II: count subarrays with sum x via prefix + hashmap, but watch long long and the empty prefix.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions both long long and initializing/handling the empty prefix.

must_hit.point: High Score: max path with ∞ if a positive cycle reaches the relevant part—Bellman-Ford plus cycle reachability, not plain shortest-path intuition.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains positive-cycle reachability implying unbounded score.

must_hit.point: Do not force knapsack DP when n≤40 subset sum calls for Meet-in-the-Middle; digit-constrained [L,R] counts need digit DP (Counting Numbers), which Striver under-covers.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects 2^n/knapsack reflex and names digit DP for adjacent-digit constraints.

must_hit.point: Tree Distances I needs diameter readiness first if rusty; rerooting/2-pass is the core pattern before stretching to Distinct Colors small-to-large / Euler+BIT.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says do diameter first, then rerooting, and treats Distinct Colors as stretch.

probes: What traps show up in Subarray Sums II, High Score, and n≤40 subset-sum style prompts?

hints.1: One numeric/prefix trap, one cycle trap, one wrong-complexity reflex.
hints.2: Prefix hashmap edge case; positive cycle on max-score; MITM vs knapsack.
hints.3: long long + empty prefix; ∞ when positive cycle reaches; n≤40 → MITM 2^{n/2}, not knapsack; digit [L,R] → digit DP.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prioritize Sorting & Searching, Range Queries, Trees, contest Graphs/DP, and MITM for OA/Div2 C–D coverage; skimming Introductory and deferring Geometry/Additional/most Advanced until cores are solid beats clearing every task.

tradeoffs.topic: Do deeply vs selective vs defer
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Deep: Sorting & Searching (STL/multiset/sweep/BS-on-answer), Range Queries (Fenwick/segtree/sparse), Trees (diameter, rerooting, LCA/binary lifting, Euler+BIT), contest Graphs (state Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford cycles, functional lifting, SCC/2-SAT later), DP gems. Selective: Mathematics and Strings beyond KMP. Defer: Geometry, Additional, Interactive, most Advanced except Meet-in-the-Middle.

tradeoffs.topic: Range structure ladder vs jumping to lazy segtree
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Enter at Dynamic Range Sum with Fenwick/segtree PURS, then segtree walk for Hotel Queries (first ≥ x); treat lazy as stretch after the core ladder prefix → sparse RMQ → Fenwick → segtree walk.

tradeoffs.topic: Knapsack/2^n DP vs Meet-in-the-Middle for subset sum
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When n≤40 and 2^n is too big, split into two halves at 2^{n/2} (CSES Meet in the Middle) instead of forcing knapsack DP.

gotchas.trap: Treating CSES like another LC grind starting at Introductory and easy Sorting warmups.
gotchas.correction: Skip/skim Introductory (maybe Gray Code / Digit Queries if weak on construction) and pure-LC Sorting warmups; start where contest form begins.

gotchas.trap: Concert Tickets: picking an arbitrary feasible ticket from the multiset.
gotchas.correction: Assign the largest ticket ≤ price via upper_bound then --it.

gotchas.trap: Subarray Sums II off-by-one or overflow when counting sum-x subarrays.
gotchas.correction: Use prefix + hashmap with long long and correctly handle the empty prefix.

gotchas.trap: High Score answered as ordinary shortest/longest path without cycle logic.
gotchas.correction: Bellman-Ford plus positive-cycle reachability: report unbounded when a positive cycle can affect the answer.

gotchas.trap: Seeing n≤40 subset sum and reaching for knapsack or full 2^n.
Jumping into Tree Distances I without diameter/rerooting basics.
gotchas.correction: Do Tree Diameter first if rusty, then rerooting/2-pass for max distance from every node.
